about: Burn bans the provinces announced, hand-curated from their own news releases. The dispatch board shows a record only on the dates it covers (the replay's Aug 25, 2025 is inside all three); on any other day it says 'not checked' and links to the province's burn-status page. Nothing here is looked up at runtime. Every record needs a source that says it; 'active' covers only the dates the sources support.

says.en: A burn ban, however, will remain in place.
says.fr: L’interdiction de brûlage demeure cependant en vigueur.

records.note: News release of the Department of Natural Resources and the Office of the Premier, 'Most restrictions on Crown land to be lifted tonight'. It supports the day it was published; the ban began earlier in August.

says.en: Nova Scotia has proclaimed a provincewide burn ban.

records.note: News release 'Provincewide Burn Ban in Effect': in place from July 30 until October 15 or until conditions improve. Lifted in all counties except Annapolis at 8 p.m. on September 26, 2025 (https://news.novascotia.ca/en/2025/09/26/provincewide-burn-ban-lifted-except-annapolis-county), so the record ends the day before. No French version of the release was found.

News release 'Fire ban in PEI including campfires': a fire closure order that bans all fires in the province, campfires included. Extended on August 25, 2025 until September 8 or further notice (https://www.princeedwardisland.ca/en/news/pei-fire-ban-extended). The site turns away automated readers, so no sentence is quoted here.

fr.label: Restrictions de brûlage de la Nouvelle-Écosse
